name: Alma Adams

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "On the 51st anniversary of Roe v. Wade, we remain committed to doing whatever it takes to achieve reproductive justice for our daughters and granddaughters… even if it means getting arrested, again."
"The #SCOTUS decision overturning Roe v. Wade is fundamentally wrong - and it's going to disproportionally harm populations that are already vulnerable."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Adams helped secure over $100 million for Emergency Rental Assistance in Charlotte and Mecklenburg County, and facilitated community events with RAMP CLT to make sure all of our neighbors in need could keep a roof over their heads during COVID-19."

"Alma Adams supports measures that will make housing more affordable and legislation that requires lenders to provide important disclosures on mortgages and housing counseling. When we support programs that lift the poor and the middle class, it makes it easier for people to afford good housing. Adams is the primary sponsor on legislation to make it easier for coronavirus relief funds to be used for Low-Income Housing Tax Credits projects. The bipartisan LIFELINE Act (H.R. 7078) would allow cities, counties, and states to use their Fiscal Recovery Fund dollars to maintain a robust pipeline of affordable housing developments."

"Demand for housing is exceeding the supply and the lack of affordable housing for many has become an epidemic. Everyone deserves decent, safe, affordable housing; anything less than this is not an option. Shelter is a basic human need, and housing is a fundamental human right. It should be a Constitutional right."

"Too many families across the country are suffering due to the housing crisis. The $8 billion in already-appropriated funds that this decision unlocks for affordable housing will be a lifeline for American families. Proud our legislation made a difference."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "I voted for the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment & Jobs Act because it will help solve the supply chain crisis and lower the cost of goods for American families. The next time a politician brings up inflation & rising prices, ask them how they voted. #BuildBackBetter"

"I voted with my Democratic colleagues to pass the Inflation Reduction Act, which will save 13 million Americans an average of $800 per year in lower health care premiums. Democrats are putting #PeopleOverPolitics to lower costs."

"Rising inflation has hit the middle class especially hard recently. Alma voted for the America Creating Opportunities for Manufacturing, Pre-Eminence in Technology, and Economic Strengthening (America COMPETES) Act (H.R. 4521), a comprehensive, strategic package aimed at addressing inflation by investing in the U.S. supply chain so that more goods are made in America, accelerating the production of U.S. made semiconductor chips which are critical for any electronics, and building our research capacity at HBCUs and other institutions of higher education to foster domestic innovation, advance global competitiveness and ensure we lead the technologies of the future."
Voted in favor of HR 5376: "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Almost 40% of borrowers with student loan debt didn't finish their degree. Now, they face the worst of both worlds: all of the debt and no degree. Canceling student loan debt will make a world of difference for them. #CancelStudentDebt"
"The Department of Education has broad administrative authority to cancel Federal student loan debt. I'm urging the Biden-Harris Administration to change lives on day one. #CancelStudentDebt"

"Why do we need to #CancelStudentDebt? Student loan debt kills jobs. Black and brown borrowers bear the brunt of our $1.6 trillion student loan debt crisis. #COVID19 has made it worse.@Ilhan, @RepPressley, and many other members of Congress are ready to fix that."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "One of the ways Alma hopes to reinstate the Voting Rights Act, end voter suppression, and expand opportunities for all Americans is by supporting and passing the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. [H.R.4]. The Act assures that the right of citizens to vote is not denied or abridged on account of race, color, or membership in a language minority group as a result of the implementation of certain qualifications or prerequisites to voting, or standards, practices, or procedures with respect to voting. This includes making sure that voting materials are available in a multitude of languages."
Rated 100% by Common Cause
Voted in favor of HR 4: "John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5746: "Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act"

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "9 years ago, the #ACA became law, expanding healthcare access for millions of Americans. Today, I’m committed to #ProtectOurCare and strengthen the ACA to ensure NC residents and Americans across the country can access affordable healthcare!"

"Health insurance needs to be affordable and available for everyone. That’s why Alma supports government discounts for insurance based upon income. She also supports tax incentives for small businesses that provide coverage for their employees, and she fought to close the Medicaid coverage gap, which would provide more than 212,000 North Carolinians access to healthcare."
"Healthcare should be a right, not a privilege."
Voted in favor of HR 1425: "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act"

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "As Chair of the Workforce Protections Subcommittee, Alma Adams’s number one focus is to expand benefits for our workers. The top priority must be expanding and strengthening our paid family leave laws in this country. Currently, the U.S. ranks near the bottom of industrialized nations in terms of its family leave, and even the laws we do have on the books are not enough to keep many people from falling through the cracks."
"Every worker deserves comprehensive, paid Family and Medical Leave."

"The Family and Medical Leave Act is an important piece of legislation, but Alma would like to see companies offer family leave benefits beyond the FMLA. Alma believes we need to set the standard for paid parental leave around the world."
Voted in favor of HR 6201: "Families First Coronavirus Response Act"
